A general stabilizer code has one binary symplectic check matrix S = (A | B): generator i acts as X on Ai and Z on Bi, Y where both. A CSS code is the special case where every row is pure X or pure Z; here every code has at least one mixed generator, and stays mixed under every single-qubit Clifford (a code that is CSS up to a Hadamard or an S on some qubits is rejected in favor of its CSS image, which belongs on the CSS board). These codes are ranked on their own board because the quantities the CSS board reads per side have no side here:

CSS boardthis board
checksH_X, H_ZS = (A | B), isotropic: A Bᵀ + B Aᵀ = 0
kn − rank H_X − rank H_Zn − rank S
distanced = min(d_X, d_Z), one witness per sideone d: the minimum Pauli weight of a nontrivial logical operator (Y counts once); one Pauli-operator witness
check weight wrow weight|Ai ∪ Bi|
kd²/n, g, tracksunchanged; the primary-track cells are computed the same way, but carry the code type, so a record here is never a record there
certificateMILP per sidenot built yet: every entry stands as d ≤
circuit tiermemory circuits per basisnot accepted yet: syndrome extraction needs a general stabilizer-measurement schedule

Symplectic doubling maps any [[n, k, d]] stabilizer code to a CSS code [[2n, 2k, d′]] with d ≤ d′ ≤ 2d, so the two boards are linked; halving that map is how the highest-rate entries here were built. See the schema, tracks, and how to submit a stabilizer code (bring S, or A and B, as an .npz).

Participate

Run it yourself, or point a coding agent at it.

git clone https://github.com/unitaryfoundation/qldpc-challenge
cd qldpc-challenge
# bring your symplectic matrix S = (A | B) as mycode.npz (key s, or a and b)
./qldpc submit mycode.npz --authors @you

It finds the distance witness, runs the verifier, and opens the PR for you.

Have an LLM or coding agent? Paste the research prompt and it runs the whole loop. Full guide

Primary tracks

Computed grid of locality × check weight, derived from H and the layout, not self-declared. Each cell lists its Pareto frontier, ranked by the selected score (kd²/n, or geometric efficiency g for codes with a verified layout); codes tied on the score rank by the lowest (n, k) pair. The code count filters the table below to that cell. Membership nests: a tighter cell’s codes also compete in the looser ones. In the g view, the seeded surface/toric tilings are not raced; they set the ceiling g is normalized to (surface code = 1) and appear dimmed below the ranking.
